---
name: diagnose-before-edit
description: Use when behavior is surprising, a fix failed, or the territory is unfamiliar — suspend edits, trace the end-to-end mechanism, and prove WHERE and WHY before changing any code.
---

# Diagnose Before Edit

When something is misbehaving or you are in unfamiliar code, do not patch the symptom. Impose a read-only gate: name and trace the mechanism first, locate the fault, and only edit once the cause is pinned to specific files. This mirrors the user's standing practice of fusing an explicit "don't write any code yet" constraint to a "help me understand how X works" demand.

## Steps

1. Treat a "step back", "don't change anything yet", "where does X happen", or "how does this work" cue (explicit or implied by a surprising bug) as a switch into read-only diagnosis. Do not edit code in this phase.
2. Trace the end-to-end mechanism and narrate it: where the value/behavior originates, every hop it takes, and where it finally renders or takes effect. Name the specific files and lines.
3. Localize the fault before proposing any fix. State which location(s) you suspect and the evidence for that localization — and check whether it could live in more than one place rather than assuming a single site.
4. State the causal chain explicitly and, when rejecting a candidate fix, supply a competing root-cause hypothesis rather than just trying again.
5. Propose how the fix will be verified, then wait for authorization before editing.
6. Only after the mechanism's home is pinned to concrete files, make the minimal change at that layer — never patch the layer where the symptom merely surfaced.

## Verification

Before editing, you should be able to answer, in writing: "The behavior is produced by `<file>:<lines>` because `<causal chain>`, and I will confirm the fix by `<observation/command>`." If you cannot, you have not finished diagnosing.

## Failure modes

- Patching the layer where the symptom appears (e.g. button-state code) when the real cause is elsewhere (a default selection upstream). The user rejects this with: "You got it wrong… the issue was not with the button states." Localize first.
- Jumping to a fix on the first plausible theory. Demand or construct the observation that would discriminate between candidate causes before committing to one.
- Editing during a "don't write any code yet" instruction. That instruction is a gate, not a delay — produce the mechanism trace and stop.

## Notes

Forged by Lore from latent practice across specstory-monorepo and stoa (2024-12 → 2026-04), consistently followed by the user, high adjacent-approval rate. Consolidates the read-before-write gate, fault-localization-before-fix, and mechanism-trace-before-trust patterns.

4312:1619:- Verdict — did-it-actually-work (§13.8/§37.11): `deadreckon verdict` is a read-only verb that re-verifies any run NOW (native or imported) into three honest states — `VERIFIED` / `REGRESSED` / `UNVERIFIED` — by re-running its acceptance checks through the gate's write-free path, reading (never overwriting) the signed marker, and diffing changed files since snapshot. A forged/tampered marker or a now-failing must-pass check reads `REGRESSED`, never a false `VERIFIED`; imported runs (Claude Code/Codex/aider) report `UNVERIFIED` with `source:"imported"`. `--all` compares recent runs, `--json` is at parity, and the only write is an additive `proofs/verdict-<ts>.json` audit sidecar never read back as authority. No `PipelineState`/`AcceptanceMarker` schema change; no run-state mutation or promotion. This closes the prior thin gap where there was no honest, after-the-fact "did it still work?" check for imported or long-finished runs.
4330:2276:`deadreckon rewind <run-id> --to-turn <n>|--to-provider-event <seq>|--to-checkpoint <id>` defaults to preview. Preview materializes the target under `<run-root>/rewind-preview/<checkpoint-id>/` and lists the files that would change. `--apply` first refuses superseded checkpoints, then hash-guards changed files against DeadReckon's latest snapshot/current checkpoint expectation before copying only the guarded changed files into the run working directory. Unrelated user edits produce a refusal in `rewind-events.jsonl`.

//! The zero-effort pipeline: `olcp up` bootstraps, ingests, and keeps
//! itself polite about money and git.

use olcp::pipeline::{self, DistillStatus};
use std::path::PathBuf;

fn fixtures() -> PathBuf {
    PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("tests/fixtures")
}

/// An export dir with the three standard fixture sessions.
fn export_dir(dir: &std::path::Path) -> PathBuf {
    let exp = dir.join("exports");
    for f in ["alpha", "beta", "gamma"] {
        let d = exp.join(f);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&d).unwrap();
        std::fs::copy(fixtures().join(f).join("session-data.json"), d.join("session-data.json"))
            .unwrap();
    }
    exp
}

#[test]
fn up_bootstraps_ingests_and_is_idempotent() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let exp = export_dir(dir.path());
    let first = pipeline::up(dir.path(), Some(&exp), Some(0), &|_| {}).unwrap();
    assert!(first.created_store, "no init ceremony");
    assert_eq!(first.sessions, 3);
    assert!(first.new_cells > 0);
    assert!(
        matches!(
            first.distill,
            DistillStatus::Deferred { .. } | DistillStatus::NoKey { .. }
        ),
        "no model call either way: {:?}",
        first.distill
    );
    // with a key present (PATH is always set) the zero guard defers the
    // backfill deterministically — still no model call
    std::fs::write(
        dir.path().join(".olcp/config.toml"),
        "[bench]\njudge_model = \"m\"\nbudgets = [500]\n\n[distill]\n\
         base_url = \"https://example.invalid\"\nmodel = \"none\"\napi_key_env = \"PATH\"\n",
    )
    .unwrap();
    let guarded = pipeline::up(dir.path(), Some(&exp), Some(0), &|_| {}).unwrap();
    assert!(
        matches!(guarded.distill, DistillStatus::Deferred { pending } if pending > 0),
        "{:?}",
        guarded.distill
    );
    // second run: nothing to do, nothing spent
    let second = pipeline::up(dir.path(), Some(&exp), Some(0), &|_| {}).unwrap();
    assert!(!second.created_store);
    assert_eq!(second.new_cells, 0, "fingerprints make re-runs free");
}
